title: Where it grows
subtitle: The Cape's own grape
objectives: Explain how it suits the Cape
Name other countries that grow it

steps.title: The Cape
steps.body: Pinotage is about 7% of South Africa's vineyards. Stellenbosch is its heartland, with Paarl, Swartland and Malmesbury also important. Bush vines on dryland, without irrigation, are valued for concentration. Old Pinotage vineyards, some from the 1950s, are now prized.

steps.title: Suited to the Cape
steps.body: Pinotage buds and ripens early, accumulating sugar fast. That's useful in warm Cape summers, but growers must pick carefully to avoid jammy fruit and high alcohol. It's vigorous and productive, so yields need control. Its thick skins give colour and resist rot.

steps.prompt: Which describe Pinotage in the vineyard?
steps.explanation: Pinotage accumulates sugar quickly, often reaching high alcohol.

steps.body: Look for Pinotage from old bush vines in Stellenbosch or Swartland. They often show more depth and less of the burnt rubber note that hurt the grape's reputation.

steps.prompt: Where else is Pinotage grown, in small amounts?
steps.explanation: Small plantings exist in New Zealand, the US, Germany and Zimbabwe, but South Africa dominates.

steps.title: What you learned
points: It ripens early and needs yield control
Small plantings exist abroad, but it's essentially South African
